name: Hazelwood Opportunity Center
notes: Currently operating HSD alternative-education center at 1865 Dunn Rd (official site lists Success Academy, Project Restart, Finish Line, and MO-OPS programs; an assistant principal has been in place since 2017, so the program predates 2017, but no founding date is published). The building itself is the original 1954 Hazelwood High School (see ALL-459 in another batch) and served as the Hazelwood Central High School Dunn Road campus until ~1977 (ALL-460) before being repurposed for district programs. Opening date of the Opportunity Center program itself not found online; school-program timeline could be confirmed via HSD administrative records. Recommend human follow-up with the district if the exact program start year matters.

name: St. Louis County School for Handicapped Children
historical_names: St. Louis County School for Handicapped Children
Special District for the Education and Training of Handicapped Children (St. Louis County)
district_operator: Special School District of St. Louis County / St. Louis County
notes: Seed's '1950s' refined: the entity this row almost certainly refers to is the countywide special-education district formally named the 'Special District for the Education and Training of Handicapped Children in St. Louis County' (per the Frank Ackerman Papers finding aid, SHSMO C3443) — today's Special School District of St. Louis County (SSD). SSD was established by voter referendum in December 1957 and began educating students in 1958; a Sept 5, 1958 St. Louis Post-Dispatch article ('Plans for School of Handicapped') covered its first purpose-built school, opened October 1961 as the Frank Ackerman School in Florissant (see ALL-478 in another batch) — matching the seed's 'Ackerman School predecessor' note. SSD continues operating today (Ackerman, Northview, Litzsinger, Neuwoehner, Southview schools). Before SSD, county children with disabilities were served by private programs such as the St. Louis Society for Crippled Children's Home Teaching Program (1938-mid-1950s, SHSMO LifeBridge Partnership records S0280). UNRESOLVED: the seed name could also denote a single physical school building rather than the district — the two interpretations can't be fully separated online, hence entity_type ambiguous_unresolved rather than administrative_district_only. If the district reading is correct this row should be treated as administrative_district_only: its yearbook-relevant member schools are Ackerman School and Northview High School (both in this seed dataset, serving the Hazelwood/Ferguson-Florissant/Jennings/Riverview Gardens area), plus Litzsinger, Neuwoehner and Southview elsewhere in the county.

name: Our Lady of Good Counsel School
historical_names: Our Lady of Good Counsel School
Our Lady of Good Counsel Parish School
district_operator: Our Lady of Good Counsel Parish / Archdiocese of St. Louis
notes: Parish chronology well documented: Our Lady of Good Counsel parish sat at 1114 Destrehan in the City of St. Louis 1894-1950, then relocated to Bellefontaine Neighbors (1100-1160 St. Cyr Rd) in 1951 per the St. Louis Genealogical Society closed-churches list; parishioner accounts confirm the school (K-8) was operating by 1954, so the school likely opened with or shortly after the parish relocation. In the 2005 archdiocesan consolidation the parish was suppressed and its territory merged with Corpus Christi, St. Pius X, St. Catherine of Alexandria, St. Jerome and part of St. Christopher into the new Holy Name of Jesus Parish at the former St. Jerome site (10235 Ashbrook Dr); parish schools were consolidated at the same time, so the OLGC school's records/students most likely passed to Holy Name of Jesus School (no seed row — left successor_school_id 'unknown' pending a matching row in another batch). Seed's '1950s' opening narrows to 1951 (probable).

name: St. Jerome School
district_operator: St. Jerome Parish / Archdiocese of St. Louis
notes: A St. Louis County Council resolution honoring St. Jerome Parish gives exact dates: parish founded March 17, 1952 (first mass August 31, 1952 in the rectory basement chapel on Chambers Road); 'St. Jerome School was opened in November, 1954 with 511 students enrolled'; the new church building at 10235 Ashbrook Dr, Bellefontaine Neighbors, opened May 21, 1961. Parish suppressed in the 2005 archdiocesan consolidation — its territory merged into the new Holy Name of Jesus Parish, located at the former St. Jerome site, so the school plant most likely continued as Holy Name of Jesus School (no seed row for that school — successor recorded 'unknown'). School-specific closing year is probable 2005 (parish merger year); not independently verified.

name: Grace Lutheran School
notes: Resolved seed's '1950s': the congregation's own history page documents that members of Grace Lutheran Church of St. Louis bought the 4.5-acre site at Hwy 367 & Chambers Road in March 1953, broke ground August 1954, and opened the Christian Day School in the chapel's ground floor in September 1955 with two teachers covering K-4. School remains open today as Grace Chapel Lutheran School (accredited by Missouri Non-Public School Accreditation Association and National Lutheran School Accreditation) at 10015 Lance Drive, Bellefontaine Neighbors, MO 63137.

name: Stormin Academy
notes: SEED NAME FLAG: 'Stormin Academy' is a misspelling — the real school is Storman Academy (also styled Storman-Stufflin School), which the City of Bellefontaine Neighbors' own history document spells 'Stormin Academy' (the likely source of the seed's spelling). Founded by Jacqueline Storman Turnage: doors opened September 7, 1981; she is described by the St. Louis American as headmistress of 'the first black-owned, non-sectarian and independent private school in the state of Missouri,' honored at the paper's 2012 Salute to Excellence gala and by a St. Louis County Council resolution. A private PK-8 school off Bellefontaine Road (historical addresses 1826 Chambers Rd and 10600 Bellefontaine Rd; currently listed at 10014 Diamond Dr). Still operating as Storman Lions Leadership Academy per the NCES Private School Universe Survey directory (~45 students, PK-8).

name: Riverview Gardens School District
notes: ADMINISTRATIVE DISTRICT — no yearbook of its own; member schools are the research targets. Per the detailed alumni-written district history (riverviewgardens1969.myevent.com): the district grew out of Science Hill School District #20 (a one-room frame school on the Gibson estate, then a 1926 two-story brick building at 805 Chambers Rd) and took the 'Riverview Gardens' name around the founding of Riverview Gardens High School in 1927 — opened_year uses 1927 as probable. Its modern boundaries were fixed in 1949 when the neighboring Moline School District #19 was annexed. District lost accreditation ~2013 and has been run by a state-appointed Special Administrative Board (STLPR, May 2010 onward); still operating ~13 schools today per rgsd.k12.mo.us and Wikipedia. Member schools include Riverview Gardens Senior High School, R. G. Central Middle School, and elementaries Danforth, Gibson, Glasgow Trails, Highland, Koch, Leamasters, Lewis and Clark, Meadows, Moline and Westview; historically also Science Hill/East Junior High, Riverview Elementary (Diamond Dr, 1926), and Turner School (Prospect Hill, the district's Black school until 1955 desegregation).

name: Hazelwood School District
notes: ADMINISTRATIVE DISTRICT — no yearbook of its own; member schools are the research targets. Founded December 10, 1949 (district's own 70th-anniversary materials, Flo Valley News) — created by consolidating thirteen rural school districts between 1949 and 1951 per the pre-trial stipulation in United States v. Hazelwood School District, 392 F.Supp. 1276 (E.D. Mo. 1975); the Hazelwood R-1 reorganization was approved in the countywide October 1951 consolidation vote (PRiME Center, St. Louis University). At formation it maintained eight schools (811 students). The thirteen predecessor rural districts named elsewhere in this seed dataset include Brown, Cold Water, Prigge/Larimore, Hyatt, Elm Grove, Pea Ridge, Columbia Bottom, Vossenkemper, Black Jack, Twillman and Melrose (see ALL-023..031, ALL-068..075, ALL-249..255 rows). Second-largest district in St. Louis County (~78 sq mi); still operating (Hazelwood Central, Hazelwood East, Hazelwood West high schools plus elementary/middle schools).

name: Hazelwood School District - Spanish Lake Schools
notes: ADMINISTRATIVE UMBRELLA — this is not a legal district or a single school; it is a grouping of Hazelwood School District campuses in the Spanish Lake/63138 area (HSD itself founded Dec 1949 — dates mirror ALL-489). Yearbook-relevant member schools in the Spanish Lake area include: Twillman Elementary (ALL-465/533), Larimore Elementary (ALL-464/534), Arrowpoint Elementary (ALL-468), East Middle School (ALL-461), Southeast Middle School (ALL-463), Hazelwood East High School (ALL-456/519/532, opened 1974), plus district program campuses in 63138 — Spanish Lake Campus (ALL-474), Discovery Hall (ALL-471), Bissell Hall (ALL-472), Lewis and Clark Hall (ALL-473), Twin Rivers (ALL-475), Fort Bellefontaine Campus (ALL-469) and Hazelwood Opportunity Center (ALL-476). Treat all archival searching at the member-school level.

name: Bellefontaine Neighbors School
historical_names: East Junior High School (later building identity)
district_operator: Science Hill District #20 / Riverview Gardens School District
notes: IDENTITY RESOLVED (probable): the unnamed 'one public school' inside Bellefontaine Neighbors at its June 1950 incorporation was the Riverview Gardens district's school at 805 Chambers Road — the alumni district history states explicitly that 'Riverview Gardens High School and Junior High School were located at 805 Chambers Road within the city limits of Bellefontaine Neighbors.' That building was constructed in 1926 as the new Science Hill (District #20) school, initially grades 1-8 and by ~1949 grades 7-12 including the high school founded there in 1927; when RGHS moved to the new Shepley Drive campus in September 1957 the Chambers Road building continued as East Junior High. closed_year 1957 reflects the building's transition out of its high-school role (probable), NOT demolition. Successor recorded as ALL-486 (Riverview Gardens Senior High School, another batch) as the continuation of its secondary-school identity. SEED FLAG: this row substantially duplicates ALL-492 'Bellefontaine Neighbors Public School' (same unnamed referent) — kept separate per no-silent-merge rule but a merge should be considered; also functionally overlaps the RGHS campus rows (ALL-486/487).

name: Gibson Elementary School
notes: Seed's '1950s' resolved: Gibson Elementary opened in the fall of 1953 on land donated by heirs of the Dr. James E. Gibson estate (alumni-written RGSD history — informal but specific, hence probable). Currently operating at 9926 Fonda Drive, Bellefontaine Neighbors — its own RGSD school page is live and the City of Bellefontaine Neighbors schools page lists it. NOTE: mailing ZIP is 63137, not 63138 as the seed suggests (seed ZIP reflects the community, not the postal address).

name: Danforth Elementary School
notes: Seed's 'Current/Historical' is now dated: on June 24, 2025 the RGSD Board of Education approved closing Danforth Elementary at the end of the 2025-26 school year following a demographic study (enrollment ~274-325, building needed ~$3.5M in repairs incl. ADA issues); a 'Danforth Farewell Tour' ran June 4, 2026, and the ~70-year-old building (hence opened ~1956, probable) is being repurposed as a community center. Students are redistributed to other RGSD elementaries (Lewis and Clark, Glasgow Trails, Highland per the redistricting plan) — no single successor school, hence 'none'. Address 1111 St. Cyr Rd, St. Louis MO 63137 — mailing ZIP is 63137, not the seed's 63138.

name: Fort Bellefontaine Military Reservation School
historical_names: Missouri Hills Home for Boys school
district_operator: City of St. Louis (1913-1986) / Missouri Division of Youth Services (1986-present)
notes: SEED FLAG: 'closed 1834' describes the military post, not a school — no evidence a school operated on the active reservation (Fort Bellefontaine's second site was vacated when troops moved to Jefferson Barracks in 1826; the City of Bellefontaine Neighbors' history doc says abandoned 1834). The educational lineage actually begins in 1913, when the City of St. Louis acquired the old fort property at 13290 Bellefontaine Rd and built a detention home and training school for boys there ('Bellefontaine Farms' / Missouri Hills Home for Boys — WPA-era buildings and the Grand Staircase date to the 1930s). St. Louis County took over most of the property in 1986; it is now the Missouri Hills campus of the Missouri Division of Youth Services, whose on-site school is 'Fort Bellefontaine Campus' (DYS, grades 6-12, ~12-20 students) — the same entity as seed rows ALL-469/ALL-470, recorded as the probable successor. opened_year 1913 marks the start of schooling on the site (probable); no yearbook-producing conventional school ever existed under the 'military reservation school' name.

name: Kinloch High School - Original Campus
notes: Seed's 1937/1976 largely confirmed. Kinloch's Black high-school program began in 1936 inside Dunbar elementary (see ALL-394/395) while the WPA-funded dedicated high school building was constructed — Wikipedia dates the school as founded 1936, the dedicated campus is the 1937 referent of this seed row ('Original Campus'). Context: Berkeley was incorporated in 1937 to carve the district's white students into a separate Berkeley School District, leaving Kinloch an all-Black segregated district. The district was annexed into Ferguson-Florissant R-II under the federal desegregation order in United States v. State of Missouri, 388 F. Supp. 1058 (E.D. Mo. 1975), affirmed 515 F.2d 1365 (8th Cir. 1975) — effective the 1975-76 school year; the plan terminated use of three Kinloch school facilities, and Kinloch High School closed in 1976 (its students were absorbed by Ferguson-Florissant schools, principally neighboring Berkeley High School — recorded as probable successor via row ALL-378). SEED FLAG: this row substantially overlaps ALL-393 and ALL-496 ('Kinloch High School' rows in other ZIPs) — kept separate per no-silent-merge rule; a coordinator-level merge should be considered.

name: Kinloch Elementary School
notes: SEED FLAG: the seed treats 'Kinloch Elementary' as a generic/umbrella name, but it was a real, distinct school — the St. Louis County Historic Buildings Inventory lists 'Kinloch Elementary School' at 5924 Hancock Avenue, constructed 1902-03 (architect G. E. Reid), later in business use; the St. Louis County Library's Kinloch local-history index references its cornerstone, and the 1975 federal desegregation order (US v. State of Missouri) names 'Kinloch Elementary' as a Kinloch District school to which lower elementary grades could be assigned — so do NOT conflate it with Dunbar School (ALL-395), the district's separate school for Black children (1913-1967). opened_year 1902 (probable; building date, coinciding with the district's 1902 creation). The district was annexed into Ferguson-Florissant R-II effective the 1975-76 school year; the court plan contemplated possibly keeping Kinloch Elementary open for lower grades, but the building eventually left school use — final closure year is unverified, so 1975 (seed's value, the annexation year) is recorded as probable. Successor: students absorbed into Ferguson-Florissant elementary schools; no single named successor found.
